blacklistabilityReview.evidence: On 2026-07-30 the full nine-chain deployment inventory was re-derived. At Ethereum block 25648350 the reUSD proxy still resolves to ShareToken implementation 0xb5276c436F65913Cd5332DE745d04feDEb4a21D4, whose Sourcify-verified ABI exposes only role-gated mint/burn with no holder blacklist, freeze, pause, or transfer hook; the Arbitrum, Base, and BNB Chain implementations are Sourcify-verified with the identical ShareToken function set, the Katana implementation 0xc84110aa47171452bacc2b6ca08ff2d862cbf968 is Sourcify-verified with the same set, and the Avalanche, Ink, Plasma, and Katana proxies all revert on blacklist(address) and paused() selector probes. The decisive surface is the Tempo TIP-20 reUSD 0x20c000000000000000000000e09a4cfec804f102: the TIP20Factory TokenCreated event at Tempo block 12906370 granted DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE to governance Safe 0x8eec10616802Ef639CA55c98ac856553fAdEfBaD, RoleMembershipUpdated logs show that Safe additionally holds PAUSE_ROLE and UNPAUSE_ROLE with no revocations through Tempo block 32484367, and getThreshold() = 3 confirms the Safe is live on Tempo. Under the TIP-20 specification, DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can immediately set the built-in always-reject policy or any TIP-403 blocklist policy via changeTransferPolicyId, and PAUSE_ROLE can halt all transfers; the current paused() = false and transferPolicyId() = 1 (always-allow) are settings, not bounds on reach. A live 3-of-5 Safe can therefore freeze or policy-block reUSD holders on Tempo today, so the asset-level direct holder-intervention posture is reviewed true (individual reach), superseding the 2026-07-15 possible.

oracleRisk.summary: reUSD is a senior NAV-based tranche token rather than a collateralized debt position, so it has no borrower health factor or oracle-triggered collateral liquidation branch.

branchApplicability.rationale: Re Protocol documents reUSD as a senior NAV-based tranche minted against accepted stablecoin deposits, with capital split between onchain liquidity and offchain Regulation 114 trust collateral. It does not create borrower-specific debt positions, collateral ratios, or oracle-triggered collateral liquidations, so CDP collateral branches are not applicable.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: reUSD has one native Ethereum issuance route and eight Chainlink CCIP burn/mint representation routes. The canonical-side CCIP BurnWithFromMintTokenPool is bridge machinery: it holds the Ethereum token MINTER_ROLE but can mint only through validated CCIP releaseOrMint flow and configured remote-chain lanes/rate limits. Its governance Safe owner, CCIP router/RMN validation path, peer mappings, rate limits, and emergency curse gate are represented below; the native InsuranceCapitalLayer remains the only collateral-backed native minter.

The SPL mint 2uxaYT1f… has decimals 9, supply 7,454,015.258947373, no freeze authority set to a program (the freeze-authority account is an unfunded system address), and mintAuthority ALGjEEQcjtJS7aQXvDPoFTLdp74t1ub9w8rVwKbsSHB2, which is an SPL multisig with numRequiredSigners 1 and numValidSigners 2. A decoded mintTo in that slot shows the live path: CCIP OffRamp offqSMQWgQud6WJz694LRzkeN5kMYpCHTpXQr3Rkcjm invokes ARM proxy RmnXLft1mSEwDgMKu2okYuHkiazxntFFcZFrrcXxYg7 and BurnMintTokenPool 41FGToCmdaWa1dgZLKFAjvmx6e6AjVTX7SVRibvsMGVB, which signs mintTo through multisig member HgkgFRLz76rJA2FBjJQQo41GkViewDngS4tpUKwTkhfo (a PDA holding no lamports or data). All four program IDs match Chainlink's published solana-mainnet CCIP directory entries for lane.offRamp, armProxy, poolPrograms.BurnMintTokenPool and router. Every mintTo in the 12-signature window sampled at the mint authority was CCIP OffRamp-driven and signed by that PDA. Control caveat, and the reason this route is not equivalent to the eight EVM CCIP legs: the 1-of-2 threshold means the second member, funded system account EsX25TxVd8Uc4CFBdqQCZM86aHw7KxxCdgLhpwrArJ8E, can mint unilaterally without CCIP. The sampled history shows no such mint, but the capability is unrevoked and the sample is not exhaustive.

routeChecks.lockboxOrEscrow: BurnWithFromMintTokenPool burns reUSD held by the pool on outbound transfers and mints only from releaseOrMint after CCIP validation; this is conserved bridge supply machinery, not a reserve lockbox or independent native collateral path.
routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: At Ethereum block 25770134, the verified pool exposed 12 supported CCIP chain selectors and a non-empty getRemotePools() mapping for each selector. The mappings include the authored Avalanche, Arbitrum, Base, BSC, Ink, Plasma, Katana, and Tempo representation lanes; getRemoteToken() mappings and getRemotePools() are owner-controlled through the verified addRemotePool/removeRemotePool/applyChainUpdates surfaces.
routeChecks.attestorQuorum: The verified BurnWithFromMintTokenPool routes releaseOrMint through the Chainlink CCIP router 0x80226fc0ee2b096224eeac085bb9a8cba1146f7d and RMN proxy 0x411de17f12d1a34ecc7f45f49844626267c75e81. The RMN implementation's isCursed() read was false at block 25770134, so no global emergency curse was active at observation time.
routeChecks.rateLimits: At block 25770134, getCurrentRateLimiterState() returned the same enabled outbound bucket for all 12 supported selectors: capacity 1000000000000000000000000 and rate 277777777777777777777; every inbound bucket was disabled. The pool also exposes owner-controlled setRateLimitConfig() and dynamic rate-limit administration. The pool's getDynamicConfig() returned rateLimitAdmin = 0 and feeAdmin = 0, leaving no separately identified non-owner admin in the observed configuration.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The Ethereum pool has deployed verified BurnWithFromMintTokenPool code, is not an EIP-1967 proxy, and exposes no pool-local pause or upgrade function. The 3-of-5 governance Safe 0x8eec10616802ef639ca55c98ac856553fadefbad owns the pool and controls its remote-pool, rate-limit, finality, hook, and dynamic configuration surfaces. Emergency halting is represented by the separate RMN curse control below; the RMNProxy owner read was 0x44835bbba9d40deda9b64858095ecfb2693c9449 and its ARM implementation was 0x0b047953451a207743fb62541b21199b95190602.

controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25770134, the pool owner() read returned governance Safe 0x8eec10616802ef639ca55c98ac856553fadefbad, typeAndVersion() returned BurnWithFromMintTokenPool 2.0.0, getToken() returned native reUSD 0x5086bf358635b81d8c47c66d1c8b9e567db70c72, and getDynamicConfig() returned Chainlink Router 0x80226fc0ee2b096224eeac085bb9a8cba1146f7d with zero separate rate-limit and fee admins. The verified non-proxy ABI exposes releaseOrMint/lockOrBurn plus owner-administered remote-pool, rate-limit, finality, hook, and dynamic-config methods. Fixed-block reads returned 12 supported CCIP selectors, a non-empty remote-pool mapping for every selector, and the authored destination pool identities; all 12 selectors had an enabled outbound bucket with capacity 1000000000000000000000000 and rate 277777777777777777777, while all inbound buckets were disabled. The pool's RMN proxy was 0x411de17f12d1a34ecc7f45f49844626267c75e81, whose ARM implementation was 0x0b047953451a207743fb62541b21199b95190602 and whose isCursed() read was false.

routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The pool has no local pause function; Chainlink's RMN emergency curse gate is reached through RMNProxy fallback. The ARMProxy owner was 0x44835bbba9d40deda9b64858095ecfb2693c9449 and getARM() returned 0x0b047953451a207743fb62541b21199b95190602; this emergency/admin identity is kept separate from the reUSD governance Safe's pool configuration authority.

controls.evidence: The CCIP pool's getRmnProxy() returned 0x411de17f12d1a34ecc7f45f49844626267c75e81 at block 25770134. RMNProxy getARM() returned 0x0b047953451a207743fb62541b21199b95190602, and the ARM implementation's isCursed() returned false. The pool-local ABI has no pause method, so this validated emergency curse gate is the scoreable pause/emergency surface for the canonical-side CCIP route.
